definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese art of arranging flowers in a disciplined and aesthetically pleasing manner.

examples.japanese: {華道|かどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}っている→習う：00479_narau⟧。

examples.english: My mother is a flower arrangement teacher.

examples.japanese: {華道|かどう}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: I study flower arrangement and tea ceremony.

notes:
COMPOUND: {華|か} (flower) + {道|どう} (way, path)

ALTERNATE NAME:
- ⟦{生|い}け{花|ばな}→生け花：05409_ikebana⟧/いけばな - more common in casual speech

MAJOR SCHOOLS:
- ⟦{池坊|いけのぼう}→池坊：noentry⟧ (Ikenobō - oldest school)
- ⟦{草月流|そうげつりゅう}→草月流：noentry⟧ (Sōgetsu)
- ⟦{小原流|おはらりゅう}→小原流：noentry⟧ (Ohara)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {華道|かどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}う→習う：00479_narau⟧ (to learn ikebana)
- {華道|かどう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧/⟦{師範|しはん}→師範：20595_shihan⟧ (ikebana teacher/master)
- {華道|かどう}⟦{教室|きょうしつ}→教室：00794_kyoushitsu⟧ (ikebana class)
- ⟦{流派|りゅうは}→流派：13365_ryuuha⟧ (school/style)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally associated with feminine refinement, but practiced by all genders. Often taught alongside ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧ (tea ceremony).
